overview: Black counters 3.d4 with ...f5, challenging e4 at once instead of the usual passive Philidor set-ups. After 4.dxe5 fxe4 5.Ng5 d5 6.e6 or 6.Nc3 White gets a strong initiative, and Black's king-side is weakened. The line is sharp and double-edged, with White generally better after accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Take on e5 and use Ng5 to hit e4 and f7
Develop Nc3 and Bc4 and exploit the open f-file and king
Play e6 at the right moment to disrupt Black's pawn chain

black_ideas.idea: Open the f-file with ...fxe4 and gain space with ...d5
Develop ...Bc5, ...Nc6 and use the queen on h4 or g5 for counterplay
Hold the e4 pawn and counterattack on the kingside

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black pawns on d5/e4 against White's e-pawn

character.notes: Direct counterattack with open files and exposed kings.

gambit.notes: Black gives the e5 pawn after 4.dxe5 fxe4 5.Ng5; White can keep the extra pawn.

soundness.notes: Dubious: White gets a clear initiative and comfortable play.

structure.notes: Open centre with open e- and f-files.

approach.notes: Rare; strong players hardly use it.

level.notes: Needs concrete lines; dubious, so not Beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: Zukertort Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: A quieter White line that avoids immediate complications.

character.reason: Early countergambit, open lines and tactics.

gambit.reason: Black gives a pawn for activity and counterplay.

soundness.reason: Strong players consider it close to refuted.

structure.reason: Open e- and f-files and a broken centre.

level.reason: Concrete tactics; dubious so never Beginner.

plans.reason: Black plays for activity and open files.
